javax.microedition.theme
Interface Theme

All Known Subinterfaces:
Skin
public interface Theme

Represents a system wide user interface theme. Applications cannot instantiate themes directly. Instead, ThemeManager is used to create new themes or obtain existing theme instances for querying.

After obtaining a reference to a theme using ThemeManager, applications can:

  • Query the metadata of the theme
  • Get information about any customizable element in the theme, including its content, such as a bitmap image that can be used for painting (except for DRM protected themes)
  • Modify the theme by replacing the content of some element with new content

Modifying a theme is subject to security permissions as detailed in Appendix B, "Recommended security practices for Java ME configurations and profiles".

Applications can change the customization of some element in a theme by creating a new element with the ElementFactory class and substituting it for an element with the specified feature and role using the updateElement methods.

All the methods in this interface that return an enumeration of elements must include only the top-level elements in the enumeration. That is, in the case of element groups, the enumeration contains references to any group elements but not to the elements within the groups.

All methods in this interface must work for all themes stored in the system, regardless of whether the theme is currently active or not.

Method Detail

commit

void commit()
            throws ModifyNotSupportedException

Commits the changes made to the theme by the application. The implementation should defer any changes to elements made using the updateElement methods until this method is called.

If the implementation does not support modify operations, this method must throw ModifyNotSupportedException immediately.

There is no transaction handling for commits in situations where the same theme is modified concurrently by more than one application.

If this method is successful, the implementation must send the themeModified event to all registered theme listeners and update the last modification date of the theme accordingly.

If there were no changes to the theme after the latest commit method call, this method does nothing.

Throws:
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
java.lang.SecurityException - if the application does not have the permission to modify appearances

getElement

Element getElement(java.lang.String feature,
                   java.lang.String role)
                   throws ElementNotFoundException

Retrieves a base element with the specified feature and role. This method uses the lookup order described in the "Concepts and terminology" section, under "Customizable element lookup".

getFeatureRoles

java.util.Enumeration getFeatureRoles(java.lang.String feature)
                                      throws ThemeException

Gets the roles defined for a feature in this theme. The roles are obtainable from the enumeration as java.lang.String instances.

If the feature is not supported by the theme (i.e. is not one of those returned by the getFeatures method), this method throws ThemeException. If the feature is supported but there are no roles defined for it, an empty enumeration is returned.

Parameters:
feature - the feature name
Returns:
an enumeration of the roles of the specified feature
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if feature is the empty string
java.lang.NullPointerException - if feature is null
ThemeException - if feature is not supported

getFeatures

java.util.Enumeration getFeatures()

Gets the features supported by this theme. The features are obtainable from the enumeration as java.lang.String instances. If there are no supported features, this method returns an empty enumeration. Each distinct feature must occur exactly once in the enumeration.

Returns:
an enumeration of features in this theme

getToolkitNames

java.lang.String[] getToolkitNames()

Get the names of toolkits that have element customizations defined in this theme. The toolkit name is assigned by this specification or some subsequent API specification that defines such a toolkit.

The toolkit is a unique identifying string. This specification defines canonical names for toolkits that were completely specified before the Mobile User Interface Customization API was finalized. Names for new toolkits are expected to be defined by the respective toolkit specifications.

Returns:
array of toolkit names, zero-length if none

updateElement

void updateElement(Element newElement)
                   throws ElementException,
                          ModifyNotSupportedException,
                          ThemeException

Updates the content of a customizable element in the base element set by replacing it with another element that has different content. The feature and role of the element to update are queried from the newElement parameter. Updates are not effective before the commit method is called.

If the implementation does not support modify operations, this method must throw ModifyNotSupportedException immediately.

If no element with the specified feature and role is found, an ElementNotFoundException must be thrown. If the implementation does not support the kind or the content of the new element, an UnsupportedContentException must be thrown. If there is a customization policy in effect and it prevents the element from being customized, an ElementNotCustomizableException must be thrown. It is recommended that the checks be made in this order.

The new element is created using the ElementFactory class. Applications can determine which element kinds and media types are supported by the implementation by using the Capabilities class.

Note that the element to update is contained in the calling instance, and the general lookup order for elements as described in the "Customizable element lookup" section of this specification is must not be used here.

It must not be possible to update the system default theme. If this method is called for the system default theme, ThemeException must be thrown.

Parameters:
newElement - the element to be updated, primed with the new content
Throws:
ElementException - a subclass depending on the situation
ElementNotFoundException - if no element with the specified feature and role is found
ElementNotCustomizableException - if the element is not customizable according to the customization policy in effect
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
UnsupportedContentException - if the kind or the content of the new element is not supported by this implementation for the feature and role
java.lang.NullPointerException - if newElement is null
ThemeException - if an attempt is made to update the system default theme, or there is an error accessing the theme data
java.lang.SecurityException - if the theme is DRM protected, or the application does not have the permission to modify appearances
See Also:
commit()

updateToolkitElement

void updateToolkitElement(Element newElement,
                          java.lang.String toolkitName)
                          throws ElementException,
                                 ModifyNotSupportedException,
                                 ThemeException

Updates the content of a customizable element of a user interface toolkit with another element that has different content. The feature and role of the element to update are queried from the newElement parameter. Updates are not effective before the commit method is called.

This method behaves like the no-argument version of updateElement, with the difference that the update is targeted to a specific toolkit, and support for the toolkit must be checked before the elements.

The value of toolkitName must be a valid canonical user interface toolkit name as described about the appearance descriptor in the "File Format Reference" section. The named toolkit must be one supported by the implementation, as indicated by the getSupportedToolkits method of the ToolkitCapabilities class.

Parameters:
newElement - the element to be updated, primed with the new content
toolkitName - the name of the user interface toolkit to update
Throws:
ElementException - a subclass depending on the situation
ElementNotFoundException - if no element with the specified feature and role is found
ElementNotCustomizableException - if the element is not customizable according to the customization policy in effect
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
UnsupportedContentException - if the kind or the content of the new element is not supported by this implementation for the specified feature and role, in the specified toolkit
ThemeException - if an attempt is made to update system default theme, or there is an error accessing the theme data
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if toolkitName is not a valid canonical UI toolkit name, or the implementation does not support the toolkit
java.lang.NullPointerException - if newElement or toolkitName is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the theme is DRM protected, or the application does not have the permission to modify appearances
See Also:
updateElement(Element), ToolkitCapabilities.getSupportedToolkits(), commit()
